=== 59475 Staff's Initial Brief on Remand (Final).docx ===
SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349
PUC DOCKET NO. 59475
COMMISSION STAFF’s initial brief on remand
Oncor Electric Delivery Company, LLC and LCRA Transmission Services Corporation (collectively, the Applicants) seek to amend their certificates of convenience and necessity for the proposed (1) Bell County East-to-Big Hill 765-kilovolt (kV) transmission line project in Docket No. 59475 and (2) Big Hill-to-Sand Lake 765-kV transmission line project in Docket No. 59182. 
On August 20, 2026, the administrative law judges (ALJs) from the State Office of Administrative Hearings (SOAH) filed a Proposal for Decision (PFD). The Public Utility Commission of Texas (Commission) considered the PFD at an open meeting on September 11, 2026, and issued an Order Remanding Proceeding to SOAH on September 18, 2026, requiring the SOAH ALJs to fully address issue numbers 11 and 13 from the Commission’s March 30, 2026, preliminary order. 
On September 22, 2026, the SOAH ALJs filed SOAH Order No. 35, requiring parties and Commission Staff (Staff) to submit briefing on remanded issue numbers 11 and 13 by October 7, 2026. Therefore, this initial brief on remand is timely filed.
REMANDED Issues
Issue No. 11: Are the proposed transmission facilities necessary to meet state or federal reliability standards?
Yes. The proposed transmission facilities are necessary to meet state and federal reliability standards. In particular, Staff agrees with the Applicants that “[t]he [p]rojects, in conjunction with other [Permian Basin Reliability Plan (PBRP)] projects, will resolve reliability criteria violations under [North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC)] Reliability Standard TPL-001.5.1 and [the Electric Reliability Council of Texas, Inc.’s (ERCOT)] planning criteria,” such that “[t]he [p]rojects are necessary to meet reliability standards established by [NERC] and ERCOT planning criteria.” 
These findings and conclusions are consistent with ERCOT’s reliability assessment in the PBRP. Specifically, under the PBRP, ERCOT’s steady‑state and dynamic reliability studies were performed in accordance with NERC TPL‑001‑5.1 and ERCOT planning criteria and identified widespread thermal and voltage violations, instances of voltage instability, and unsolved power flow conditions under system‑intact (N‑0) and contingency scenarios. These results demonstrate that the existing transmission system cannot reliably support current or forecasted demand and that the proposed projects are necessary to ensure a reliable transmission system. More particularly, ERCOT concluded that a 765-kV backbone solution is needed to increase import capability into the Permian Basin and to support reliable service.
Beyond the PBRP, ERCOT’s subsequent reliability assessments in the 2024 Regional Transmission Plan (RTP), the 2024 RTP 345-kV Plan and Texas 765-kV Strategic Transmission Expansion Plan Comparison, the 2025 RTP, and ERCOT’s exit strategies for the North-to-Far-West and South-to-Far-West Import Generic Transmission Constraints demonstrate that ERCOT has consistently determined that the PBRP 765-kV import paths are necessary to meet state and federal reliability standards. Indeed, throughout each of these reliability assessments and similar to its assessment under the PBRP, ERCOT evaluated reliability criteria violations and determined that the 765-kV backbone solution, including Import Path 2, was needed. Therefore, based on ERCOT’s reliability assessments, these two projects for Import Path 2 qualify as reliability projects under 16 Texas Administrative Code (TAC) § 25.101(b)(3)(A)(ii).
Issue No. 13: What is the estimated congestion cost savings for consumers that may result from the proposed transmission facilities considering both current and future expected congestion levels and the ability of the proposed transmission facilities to reduce those congestion levels? 
Because Staff recommends that the projects qualify as reliability projects under 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(A)(ii), it is not necessary to assess whether the projects also qualify as economic projects under 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(A)(i). Notably, “under the Commission’s rules, applications for transmission line projects must demonstrate need as an economic project—unless the project can qualify as a reliability project or a resiliency project.” Accordingly, an evaluation of the estimated congestion cost savings for consumers under 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(A)(i)(I) is not necessary. 
However, to the extent the SOAH ALJs disagree with Staff on issue number 11, the record evidence demonstrates that congestion cost savings may result from the projects.  Notably, based on ERCOT’s 2024 RTP 345-kV Plan and Texas 765-kV Strategic Transmission Expansion Plan Comparison, both the 345-kV Plan and the 765-kV Plan provide for congestion cost savings when compared to the base case for the 2034 study year, while only the 765-kV Plan provides for congestion cost savings when compared to the base case for the 2039 study year. So, while the 345-kV Plan provides more savings than the 765-kV Plan for the 2034 study year, the 765-kV Plan, including these two projects for Import Path 2, provides more savings in the long term. 
Beyond the estimated congestion cost savings, the record also demonstrates that, for the 2034 and 2039 study years, both the 345-kV Plan and the 765-kV Plan reduce congestion rent, while the 765-kV Plan itself results in even less congestion rent than the 345-kV Plan. These reductions are important because “[t]he area spanned by the proposed [projects] experiences significant transmission congestion, which costs ERCOT ratepayers hundreds of millions of dollars each year.” When considered together with the additional transmission capacity that would be added through the 765-kV Plan, the resulting reductions in congestion rent reflected in ERCOT’s economic studies indicate that the 765-kV Plan, including these two projects for Import Path 2, will help reduce congestion levels and thereby reduce congestion costs for consumers. 
Conclusion
Based on the foregoing discussion, Staff recommends that the proposed projects comprising Import Path 2 are necessary to meet state and federal reliability standards, and that, as a result, it is not necessary to assess whether the projects also qualify as economic projects. However, as necessary, Staff otherwise recommends that the proposed projects comprising Import Path 2 are supported from an economic standpoint.

Dated: October 7, 2026

Respectfully submitted,
